correctness.rationale: Boben–Gévay–Pisanski Lemma 4.5 identifies the exact 15-by-20 subset inclusion matrix. From the counted identity BB^T=2I+N^TN and NN^T=4I+J, the 35-vertex Laplacian eigenvalues and determinant follow exactly. The standard-library verifier reconstructs both reduced matrices, obtains exact integer cofactor 377913600000000 and performs invertible p-adic row/column elimination over Z/p^9, with all pivot valuations at most two. Both roots give valuation multiplicities 2:(24,6,4), 3:(28,2,4), 5:(26,8,0), forcing factors 1^24,2^2,10^2,30^2,180^4; independent SymPy SNF and characteristic polynomial agree. Only the 35-vertex case, under stated genericity and smoothing hypotheses, is proved.

originality.rationale: Literature establishes the classical 20-point/15-line incidence and dual realization; the newly claimed object is the complete integral Smith form of its 35-vertex graph Laplacian. The closest subset-matrix literature gives a rectangular incidence-matrix diagonal form or one-rank association-scheme graph Laplacians. Those statements do not themselves supply the mixed-rank block Laplacian invariant factors; same-size/parameter coverage was checked explicitly. An own previous Pascal graph has 105 vertices with different incidence. No matching whole-group statement was identified, subject to unindexed-graph-table priority risk.
residual_risks: Unindexed critical-group tables for the unique {35,2} biregular graph could contain an equivalent result.
A stronger general integer block-matrix theorem could implicitly specialize to this computation; the reviewed rectangular and single-rank theorems do not explicitly do so.
Only the generic characteristic-zero projective configuration and unit-thickness semistable interpretation are claimed; no positive-characteristic collision classification is established.

value.rationale: The invariant is the full degree-zero divisor class group of the canonical symmetric, edge-transitive (20_3,15_4) Steiner–Plücker incidence graph (also the Cayley–Salmon dual), not an arbitrary numerical slice. Its order and rational spectrum do not fix its integral invariant factors. The exact 5-primary rank-eight torsion and exponent 180 are intrinsically interpretable and give precise Néron geometric component groups for genus-26 unit-thickness semistable degenerations. The result is a natural complete invariant of one historically significant configuration; no broader theorem is claimed.
